theory.overview: Binary Search Tree (BST) is a binary tree where for each node, all values in left subtree are less than node's value, and all values in right subtree are greater. This property enables efficient search, insert, and delete operations in $O(\log n)$ average time (balanced tree) or $O(n)$ worst case (skewed tree). BSTs are fundamental data structures used in databases, file systems, and as building blocks for balanced trees (AVL, Red-Black). This chapter covers BST operations, traversal, and common problems.

sections.title: BST Properties
sections.content: BST invariant: for any node, left subtree values < node value < right subtree values. This enables binary search: compare target with root, go left if smaller, right if larger. In-order traversal yields sorted order. Height determines performance: balanced tree height $O(\log n)$, skewed tree height $O(n)$. BST is not guaranteed to be balanced—insertion order affects shape.
sections.invariant: left < node < right for all nodes

sections.title: BST Operations
sections.content: Search: $O(h)$ where h is height. Compare with root, go left/right recursively. Insert: $O(h)$. Search for position, insert as leaf. Delete: $O(h)$. Three cases: leaf (just remove), one child (replace with child), two children (replace with inorder successor or predecessor, then delete that node).
deleteCases: Two children: replace with inorder successor

sections.title: BST Traversals
sections.content: In-order (left, root, right): yields sorted order. Pre-order (root, left, right): useful for copying tree. Post-order (left, right, root): useful for deleting tree (delete children before parent). Level-order (BFS): process level by level. All traversals are $O(n)$ time, $O(h)$ space for recursion stack.

sections.title: BST Applications
sections.content: Database indexes: B-trees (generalization of BST) for efficient range queries. Symbol tables: compilers use BSTs for variable lookup. Priority queues: BST can implement (though heaps are more efficient). Sorting: in-order traversal of BST built from unsorted data. Range queries: find all values in range [a, b].

sections.title: BST vs Balanced Trees
sections.content: BST: $O(\log n)$ average, $O(n)$ worst. No guaranteed balance. Simple implementation. AVL tree: $O(\log n)$ guaranteed. Maintains balance factor (height difference ≤ 1). Rotations on insert/delete. Red-Black tree: $O(\log n)$ guaranteed. Color-based balancing. Simpler than AVL. Used in many standard libraries.

keyConcepts.name: BST Invariant
keyConcepts.description: For every node: left subtree values < node value < right subtree values. This property enables binary search.

keyConcepts.name: Height
keyConcepts.description: Height of tree = length of longest path from root to leaf. Balanced BST height = $O(\log n)$, skewed = $O(n)$. Performance depends on height.
keyConcepts.formula: Height of balanced tree with n nodes ≈ $\log_2 n$

keyConcepts.name: Inorder Successor
keyConcepts.description: Next node in in-order traversal. For node with right child: leftmost in right subtree. Without right child: first ancestor where node is in left subtree.
keyConcepts.use: Delete operation, finding next greater element

keyConcepts.name: Recursion
keyConcepts.description: BST operations naturally recursive. Base case: null node. Recursive case: operate on left/right subtree. Stack depth = tree height.

steps.title: Search
steps.description: Compare target with root. If equal, return. If target < root, search left. Else search right.
steps.code: if root == null: return null; if target == root.val: return root; if target < root.val: return search(root.left); return search(root.right);

steps.title: Insert
steps.description: Search for insertion point (null). Insert as new node at that position.
steps.code: if root == null: return new Node(val); if val < root.val: root.left = insert(root.left, val); else: root.right = insert(root.right, val); return root;

steps.title: Find Min/Max
steps.description: Min: go left until null. Max: go right until null.
steps.code: def find_min(node): while node.left: node = node.left; return node;

steps.title: Delete - Two Children
steps.description: Find inorder successor (min in right subtree). Replace node with successor. Delete successor from right subtree.
steps.code: successor = find_min(root.right); root.val = successor.val; root.right = delete(root.right, successor.val);

steps.title: Traverse
steps.description: In-order: traverse left, visit root, traverse right. Yields sorted order.
steps.code: def inorder(node): if node: inorder(node.left); visit(node); inorder(node.right);

practiceProblems.title: Validate BST
practiceProblems.description: Check if binary tree is valid BST.
practiceProblems.solution: In-order traversal with min/max bounds. For each node, check if value in (min, max). Recurse with updated bounds.
practiceProblems.hints: Pass min/max bounds, check if node value in range

practiceProblems.title: Search in BST
practiceProblems.description: Search for value in BST, return node or null.
practiceProblems.solution: Recursive or iterative. Compare with root, go left if smaller, right if larger.
practiceProblems.hints: Binary search: compare, go left or right

practiceProblems.title: Insert into BST
practiceProblems.description: Insert value into BST, return root.
practiceProblems.solution: Search for null position, insert as leaf. Recursive or iterative.
practiceProblems.hints: Find null position, insert as leaf

practiceProblems.title: Delete from BST
practiceProblems.description: Delete node with given value from BST.
practiceProblems.solution: Three cases: leaf (remove), one child (replace with child), two children (replace with inorder successor).
practiceProblems.hints: Handle three cases: leaf, one child, two children

practiceProblems.title: Kth Smallest Element
practiceProblems.description: Find kth smallest element in BST.
practiceProblems.solution: In-order traversal, count nodes. Return when count == k. Or use augmented nodes with left subtree size.
practiceProblems.hints: In-order traversal, count until k

practiceProblems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor
practiceProblems.description: Find LCA of two nodes in BST.
practiceProblems.solution: If both nodes < root, LCA in left. If both > root, LCA in right. Else root is LCA.
practiceProblems.hints: Use BST property to narrow search

practiceProblems.title: Convert Sorted Array to BST
practiceProblems.description: Convert sorted array to height-balanced BST.
practiceProblems.solution: Recursively pick middle as root, build left from left half, right from right half.
practiceProblems.hints: Middle element as root, recurse on halves

practiceProblems.title: Balanced BST
practiceProblems.description: Check if BST is height-balanced (|height(left) - height(right)| ≤ 1 for all nodes).
practiceProblems.solution: Recursively check balance, return height. If any subtree unbalanced, propagate -1.
practiceProblems.hints: Return height, check balance at each node

practiceProblems.title: Inorder Successor
practiceProblems.description: Find inorder successor of given node in BST.
practiceProblems.solution: If right child exists: leftmost in right subtree. Else: traverse up until node is left child of parent.
practiceProblems.hints: Right child: leftmost in right. No right: first ancestor where node is left child

practiceProblems.title: Range Sum of BST
practiceProblems.description: Sum of all node values in range [low, high].
practiceProblems.solution: In-order traversal. If node value < low, only go right. If > high, only go left. Else sum node and recurse both sides.
practiceProblems.hints: Prune: if value < low, skip left; if > high, skip right

practiceProblems.title: Two Sum IV - Input is BST
practiceProblems.description: Find if two elements in BST sum to k.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash set during traversal. For each node, check if k - node.val in set. Add node.val to set.
practiceProblems.hints: Hash set, check complement during traversal

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Absolute Difference
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum absolute difference between any two nodes in BST.
practiceProblems.solution: In-order traversal (sorted). Track previous value, compute min difference with current.
practiceProblems.hints: In-order gives sorted order, compare consecutive

practiceProblems.title: Find Mode in BST
practiceProblems.description: Find mode(s) (most frequent value) in BST.
practiceProblems.solution: In-order traversal. Track current value count, max count, and modes list.
practiceProblems.hints: In-order, track count of current value

practiceProblems.title: Convert BST to Greater Tree
practiceProblems.description: Convert BST so each node value = sum of all values greater than or equal to original.
practiceProblems.solution: Reverse in-order (right-root-left). Maintain running sum, add to each node.
practiceProblems.hints: Reverse in-order, maintain running sum

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
practiceProblems.description: Iterative in-order traversal (no recursion).
practiceProblems.solution: Stack. Push all left nodes. Pop, visit, push right subtree's left nodes.
practiceProblems.hints: Stack simulates recursion, push all left first

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
practiceProblems.description: Iterative preorder traversal.
practiceProblems.solution: Stack. Push root. While stack: pop, visit, push right then left (left processed first).
practiceProblems.hints: Stack: push right then left (LIFO)

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
practiceProblems.description: Iterative postorder traversal.
practiceProblems.solution: Two stacks or one stack with visited flag. Or modify tree (reverse preorder then reverse result).
practiceProblems.hints: Two stacks or reverse preorder

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Level Order
practiceProblems.description: Level order traversal (BFS).
practiceProblems.solution: Queue. Enqueue root. While queue: process level (all nodes in queue), enqueue children.
practiceProblems.hints: Queue for BFS, process all nodes at current level

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
practiceProblems.description: Return right side view of binary tree (nodes visible from right).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS, take last node of each level. Or DFS with depth, take first node at each depth from right.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS: last node of each level. DFS: rightmost at each depth

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Vertical Order
practiceProblems.description: Return vertical order traversal (group nodes by column index).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS with column index. Hash map: column → list of (row, value). Sort by row within each column.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS with column index, hash map by column

practiceProblems.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order
practiceProblems.description: Zigzag level order (left to right, then right to left, alternating).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS with direction flag. Reverse every other level's result.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS, reverse every other level

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
practiceProblems.description: Find maximum depth (height) of binary tree.
practiceProblems.solution: Recursive: 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). Or BFS counting levels.
practiceProblems.hints: Recursive: 1 + max of children depths

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum depth (shortest path to leaf).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS. Return level when first leaf found. Or recursive with null child handling.
practiceProblems.hints: BFS returns first leaf level

practiceProblems.title: Symmetric Tree
practiceProblems.description: Check if tree is symmetric (mirror of itself).
practiceProblems.solution: Recursive: compare left.left with right.right, left.right with right.left.
practiceProblems.hints: Compare mirror positions recursively

practiceProblems.title: Path Sum
practiceProblems.description: Check if root-to-leaf path sums to target.
practiceProblems.solution: Recursive: subtract node value from target, check if leaf with target 0.
practiceProblems.hints: Subtract value, check leaf with target 0

minigame.description: Build and manipulate BSTs! Insert, search, and traverse interactively.
